clue.text: Moist fine-grained earth in small measure – just the opposite

indicators.text: in small measure – just the opposite
indicators.note: the surface puts the earth inside the measure, and 'just the opposite' flips that, so the measure goes inside the earth

blocks.note: clay is soil made of very fine particles
mm, the millimetre, is a tiny unit of length

explanation.surface: A soil scientist describes a damp sample of fine soil, measured in small quantities.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the earth would sit inside the measure; 'just the opposite' reverses which piece holds which.
explanation.definitionFit: Clammy describes something unpleasantly damp and sticky to the touch, a close synonym.

clue.text: Reduce support after snub

indicators.note: after places the support word behind the snub word in the answer

blocks.note: to cut someone is to snub or ignore them
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Funding is reduced after a public snub.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut back is a phrasal verb meaning to reduce spending or amounts.

clue.text: Fellow not born sharp-witted

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter standing for born is dropped

blocks.note: Albert is a man's name, any fellow
b is the abbreviation for born

explanation.surface: A man not naturally gifted is nonetheless quick-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert means quick to notice and respond, a near synonym of mentally sharp.

clue.text: John Pilger's one friend possesses interminable spirit

indicators.note: interminable means without end, so the last letter of the drink is cut
possesses means holds, so the friend word surrounds the shortened drink

blocks.note: mucker is British slang for a mate or pal
raki is an aniseed spirit from Turkey and the Balkans

explanation.surface: John Pilger has a single friend who is gripped by an everlasting spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: John Pilger was an Australian investigative journalist; 'one' turns him into an example, one such journalist exposing scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A muckraker is a journalist who digs up scandal and corruption, as Pilger did in exposés.

clue.text: Tender prince removed from queen

blocks.note: Pr is a standard abbreviation for prince
off means taken away or removed
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A royal prince is taken away from the queen's side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' is a verb here, to offer, not the adjective for soft or loving.
explanation.definitionFit: To proffer is to hold out or offer something, just as you tender a payment or resignation.

clue.text: Supporter's depression to stop suddenly

blocks.note: a pit is a hollow or depression in the ground
a horse props when it stops dead with its forelegs rigid

explanation.surface: A supporter's spirits sink, to stop suddenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low mood, but here it is a hollow in the ground; the 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit prop is a timber post supporting the roof of a mine, literally a supporter.

clue.text: Politician oddly okay over hoax

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third and other odd-placed letters
over means spread across, so the two kept letters sit either side of the hoax

blocks.note: the odd-placed letters of okay
bam is an old word for a hoax or trick

explanation.surface: A politician strangely approves of a deception.
explanation.definitionFit: Barack Obama was US president, so he is an example of a politician.

clue.text: Gun wounds are dressed with it during flight

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the dressing sits inside the flight

blocks.note: a flight of birds is a flock
lint is soft fabric used for dressing wounds

explanation.surface: A gunshot victim's wounds are dressed while fleeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests escape, but it is a group of birds in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A flintlock is an old firearm fired by a flint striking steel, so it is a gun.

clue.text: Engineers need to avoid being careless

blocks.note: the RE, Royal Engineers, are a corps of the British Army
to miss something is to avoid it

explanation.surface: Engineers must not be careless.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent in one's duty, a formal synonym for careless.

clue.text: Mother getting better after bit of detergent causes rash

indicators.note: a bit of the word means only its first letter is taken
after places the word for getting better behind the single letter

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
the first letter of detergent
to cap is to outdo or better something

explanation.surface: Mother recovers but a soap product gives her a skin rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' suggests an itchy skin reaction to the detergent; it is the adjective meaning reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Madcap describes someone wildly impulsive or reckless, which is what rash means as an adjective.

clue.text: Cutting about new song by tenor

indicators.note: by means beside, so the voice part is placed next to the other pieces, here at the front

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for tenor in music
re means about or concerning
N is the abbreviation for new
a chant is a simple sung melody

explanation.surface: A reviewer is scathing about a fresh song performed by a tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant remarks are incisive and sharp, so cutting is a close synonym used figuratively.

clue.text: Nothing to stop silent movie star coming back after initially agreeing in principle

indicators.note: initially points at the first letter only of the word it follows
coming back means the star's name is read from right to left
to stop a gap is to plug it, so the nothing is pushed into the middle of the name
after places the first piece in front of everything else in the answer

blocks.note: the first letter of agreeing
Tom Mix was a cowboy star of silent films
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An agreement in principle depends on a silent-film star returning, with nothing standing in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Mix, a silent-era Western hero, is the star; his name turned round takes O inside before the A goes on the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a self-evident truth taken as a basic principle on which reasoning rests.

clue.text: Mother, miles away, taking in fellow's behind

indicators.note: away means removed, so the abbreviation for miles is taken out
taking in means absorbing, so the shortened word wraps around another piece

blocks.note: mater is Latin for mother, used in old public-school slang
M is the abbreviation for miles
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: Mum, far away, puts up a fellow who is running late.
explanation.walkthrough: MATER loses its M to leave ATER, which then takes F inside; the 's is short for is, joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: After and behind both mean later in sequence or following on, as in coming after someone.

clue.text: Worker absorbed in revolutionary verse by Cuba's top writer

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests overthrow and upheaval, so the poem's letters are thrown into a new order
absorbed in means taken inside, so the worker sits within the other letters
top in an across clue means the first letter of the word
by means next to, joining the single letter to the rest

blocks.note: the first letter of Cuba
the five letters of verse rearranged
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A worker steeped in the revolutionary poetry of Cuba's finest writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuba and 'revolutionary' suggest Castro or Guevara, but the writer is the Spanish author of Don Quixote.
explanation.definitionFit: Miguel de Cervantes was the Spanish novelist who wrote Don Quixote, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Buffet at college is put together hurriedly

blocks.note: to buffet is to strike or knock
a student in residence at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: A college buffet is thrown together in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' looks like a spread of food that fits the hurried meal, but it is the verb to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock up something is an idiom for making it quickly from whatever is to hand.

clue.text: Convenient for a country girl off to the Newcastle area after work

indicators.note: off means removed, so a word for girl is taken out of the country
after places the remaining pieces behind the word for work

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
Portugal is a country of Iberia
gal is informal for a girl
Newcastle is in the North East of England

explanation.surface: A country girl finds it convenient to head off to Newcastle after work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A country girl' reads as a rural lass, but splits into a country and a girl to remove from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune means well-timed and suitable, so convenient is a close synonym.

clue.text: Nick finds Penny omitting opening of prayer

indicators.note: omitting the opening means the first letter of the word is dropped
finds links the coin to what follows, setting the pieces side by side

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny
an orison is an old word for a prayer

explanation.surface: Nick finds that Penny has left out the start of her prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick and Penny look like two people; nick is British slang for a police station or jail.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the nick is a jail, so it is an informal synonym for a place of confinement.

clue.text: Oddly neglected film misrepresenting Titian over forgery

indicators.note: neglecting the odd letters leaves just the even-placed ones
misrepresenting means showing falsely, so the painter's letters are presented in a wrong order

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of film
the letters of Titian plus O, over in cricket, rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange film misrepresents Titian and passes off a forgery.
explanation.walkthrough: Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter; O is the cricket abbreviation for an over.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitation is a copy passed off as the real thing, so it can be a forgery.

clue.text: Runs around embracing current enthusiasm

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the word for runs is read backwards
embracing means holding inside, so one letter is wrapped by the rest

blocks.note: trips are short journeys or runs, as in a run to the shops
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone runs around hugging the latest craze with great zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs around' reads as one phrase but splits: TRIPS turned round gives SPIRT, which then holds the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit means liveliness and zeal, as in entering into the spirit, so it matches enthusiasm.

clue.text: Time to face money problems

definitions.note: plural noun defining a mass noun

indicators.note: to face means to stand in front of, so the time letter comes first

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
the rouble is the Russian unit of currency

explanation.surface: It is time to confront one's money worries.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble means difficulties or worries, so it stands for problems collectively.

clue.text: Girl starts to embroider name in yellow

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters of the next two words are taken

blocks.note: chick is informal slang for a young woman
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A girl begins sewing a name in yellow thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow' looks like a colour of thread; it means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow and chicken are both informal adjectives meaning cowardly or lacking nerve.

clue.text: Keep outlaw's heart enclosed in box

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the middle letters are kept
enclosed in means held within, so the middle letters go inside the box word

blocks.note: a case is a box or container
the middle two letters of outlaw

explanation.surface: A robber's heart is locked away in a strongbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb, to retain, but it is a noun: the stronghold of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the fortified central tower of a castle, so the two words name related strongholds.

clue.text: One needing no introduction is after my French goddess

indicators.note: no introduction means without its first letter, so the word loses its start
after places the remaining pieces behind the shortened number word

blocks.note: taken as written
mes is French for my, with plural nouns
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrity who needs no introduction follows my French goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, punishing hubris.

clue.text: Girl's turning against conservationists in authority

indicators.note: turning means turning round, so the girl's name and its s are read backwards
against means up next to, so the two parts are set side by side

blocks.note: Ava is a girl's name, with 's adding S
the NT, National Trust, conserves British heritage sites

explanation.surface: A girl turns against the conservationists in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' looks like opposition but just means beside; the National Trust looks after historic houses and countryside in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a learned person, an expert whose word carries weight as an authority.

clue.text: Awful for co-star worried about debt

indicators.note: worried suggests being disturbed and agitated, so the star's letters are shaken into a new order
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the debt

blocks.note: the six letters of co-star rearranged
an IOU is a written note acknowledging a debt

explanation.surface: An actor feels terrible for a co-star fretting over money owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrocious means extremely bad or dreadful, so awful is a direct synonym.

clue.text: A body part from the man is exhibited in court

indicators.note: exhibited in means displayed within, so the words go inside the court abbreviation

blocks.note: Ct is the abbreviation for court
he's is the contraction of he is

explanation.surface: A body part taken from the man is displayed as evidence in court.
explanation.definitionFit: The chest is the front of the torso between neck and abdomen, a part of the body.

clue.text: Soldiers endlessly going around city warning of danger

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter of the soldiers' word is cut

blocks.note: an army is a body of soldiers

explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a signal such as a bell or siren that alerts people to danger.

clue.text: 11 French letters belonging to Maria presumably

indicators.note: letters belonging to the following words means the answer is found inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: French letters written by Maria, presumably.

clue.text: Entertain with new masque after queen leaves

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the letter for queen is removed from the word
new suggests something remade, so the remaining letters are arranged afresh

explanation.walkthrough: A masque is itself a courtly entertainment, which makes the surface hang together neatly.

clue.text: Head of Leweston having trouble getting back in time before school's first game

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the school's name
getting back means returning, so the word for trouble runs right to left
having means accompanied by, joining the two small pieces together
in places the joined pieces inside the word for a spell of time
first means only the opening letter of school is taken

blocks.note: the first letter of Leweston
to ail is to trouble or afflict
bird is British slang for a prison sentence
the first letter of school

explanation.surface: The head of Leweston, a Dorset school, struggles to get back in time for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: L and LIA go inside BIRD, then S closes it. Doing bird is British slang for serving a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: Billiards is a cue game played on a cloth-covered table, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Mata essentially seen inside in that position where Finney played

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so only the central letters are taken
inside means within, so the central letters sit in the other word

blocks.note: there means in that place or position
the middle two letters of Mata

explanation.surface: Mata Hari is spotted inside, in the place where Albert Finney once performed.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Finney was an English actor who began on stage, so the definition describes a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre is a building where plays are performed, the venue for an actor such as Finney.

clue.text: Carol rings in due course about discovering spiritual knowledge

indicators.note: in signals insertion, and due course loosely says the rings go in along the way
about means turned around, so the whole word is read backwards

blocks.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
rings are Os, the plural of the letter O, written here back to front

explanation.surface: A choir sings in due course about finding spiritual enlightenment.
explanation.walkthrough: The rings are two letter Os; 'in due course' is a loose insertion signal, the rings going in once the carol is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnosis is esoteric knowledge of spiritual truths, the insight prized by the ancient Gnostics.
